name: Ahaziah
overview: Ahaziah was a male member of the tribe of Judah who served as king of Judah. He was the youngest son of Jehoram, himself a descendant of Jehoshaphat. His reign was brief and marked by negative influences, reflecting the challenges of his royal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahaziah means 'YHWH has upheld,' indicating a connection to God's sustaining power. He was also known by the names Jehoahaz, meaning 'YHWH holds,' and Azariah, meaning 'YHWH has helped.' These names reflect various aspects of divine support, though none are explicitly given by God. His title as King of Judah identifies his royal position.
familyAndRelationships: Ahaziah was the son of Jehoram and Athaliah, and he had a brother named Jehosheba. Additionally, he was the father of Joash. These relationships situate him within the royal family of Judah and link him to significant biblical figures.
scriptureSignificance: Ahaziah's significance lies in his role as a young king whose short reign was heavily influenced by his mother, leading him to follow the sinful practices associated with the house of Ahab. His alliance with Joram of Israel against Syria and subsequent death at the hands of Jehu highlight the consequences of ungodly associations and the swift judgment that can follow. His story serves as a sobering example of how quickly evil influence can corrupt and bring about divine judgment.
